overview: SimpleTIR stabilizes multi-turn tool-integrated reasoning (TIR) training under Zero RL by identifying and filtering trajectories containing 'void turns' (responses with neither complete code blocks nor final answers), thereby blocking harmful high-magnitude gradients caused by distributional drift from external tool feedback, achieving state-of-the-art performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

modules.name: Hierarchical MDP Environment
modules.description: Implementation of the multi-turn TIR environment modeled as a Hierarchical Markov Decision Process, separating turn-level high-level MDP (governing conversation strategy with states as conversation history and terminal rewards) and token-level low-level MDP (governing individual token generation within each turn with zero intrinsic reward), supporting unified policy training across both levels.

modules.name: Asynchronous Code Execution Sandbox
modules.description: Implementation of an asynchronous code interpreter sandbox (using SandboxFusion) that executes Python code blocks generated by the LLM, captures stdout/stderr output, handles timeouts and runtime errors, and returns execution results with the 'Code Execution Result:' prefix, ensuring strict halting of LLM generation after complete code blocks and appending true external tool feedback.

modules.name: Multi-Turn Rollout Manager
modules.description: Orchestration of multi-turn interaction rollouts between the LLM agent and the code execution environment, managing turn-by-turn generation with configurable maximum turns (starting from 5, scaling to 10), concatenating tool feedback into subsequent prompts, prepending 'final_answer' function shortcuts before code blocks, and collecting complete trajectory sequences of (response, feedback) pairs.

modules.name: Feedback Token Masking
modules.description: Implementation of binary masking over trajectories to exclude environment-provided tool feedback tokens from policy loss computation, ensuring correct credit assignment by accumulating loss only over timesteps corresponding to agent-generated response tokens, while preserving the causal influence of feedback on subsequent generation probabilities.

modules.name: Void Turn Detector
modules.description: Detection logic that inspects each turn in a generated trajectory to identify 'void turns' — LLM responses that contain neither a complete executable code block (valid triple-backtick-wrapped Python with imports) nor a final answer (boxed expression or final_answer call), serving as a heuristic indicator of distributional drift and pathological low-probability generation.

modules.name: SimpleTIR Trajectory Filter
modules.description: The core innovation module that filters out entire trajectories containing at least one void turn before policy gradient computation, simultaneously blocking harmful high-magnitude gradients from low-probability token sequences and correcting misaligned credit assignment by ensuring successful early turns are not penalized for later collapses, acting as a plug-and-play component compatible with any RL algorithm.

modules.name: GRPO Training Loop with TIR Loss
modules.description: Implementation of Group Relative Policy Optimization integrating feedback masking and trajectory filtering, computing advantage estimates as relative performance within groups of trajectories sampled from the same prompt, applying the clipped surrogate PPO objective only on unmasked response tokens from valid (non-void) trajectories, with configurable group size, PPO clip ratios (asymmetric low/high), and PPO epochs per update.

modules.name: Gradient Norm and Token Probability Monitor
modules.description: Real-time monitoring and diagnostic module tracking gradient norms and minimum token probabilities across training steps, implementing the theoretical analysis from Proposition 1 (L2 norm of policy gradient w.r.t. pre-softmax logits) to detect distributional drift and gradient explosion events, logging correlations between low-probability tokens and gradient spikes for training stability analysis.

modules.name: Training Data Pipeline
modules.description: Data preprocessing and loading pipeline for mathematical reasoning datasets (Math3-5 from SimpleRL and Deepscaler), implementing prompt formatting for base models without chat templates, constructing the multi-turn TIR prompt template emphasizing Python code in triple backticks with imports, explicit print statements for intermediate results, and standardized answer channels (final_answer or boxed), with rollout batch sampling and per-prompt group generation.

modules.name: Outcome Reward Computation
modules.description: Implementation of sparse terminal reward computation for mathematical reasoning tasks, extracting final answers from LLM responses (parsing boxed expressions or final_answer function outputs) and comparing against ground truth with appropriate mathematical equivalence checking, assigning unit reward at trajectory termination with no per-step intrinsic rewards.

modules.name: Dynamic Response Length and Turn Scaling
modules.description: Training workflow control that dynamically adjusts maximum response length (starting at 16K tokens, scaling to 24K) and maximum interaction turns (starting at 5, scaling to 10) based on training progress, specifically when average response length plateaus, enabling progressive scaling of reasoning complexity without early truncation of valid trajectories.

modules.name: Benchmark Evaluation Pipeline
modules.description: Comprehensive evaluation on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (Math500, AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, Hmmt Feb 25) with temperature-1 sampling and average@32 score reporting for variance reduction, supporting both TIR-enabled and text-only evaluation modes, and automated comparison against baseline categories: non-TIR Zero RL, cold-start TIR RL, and Zero RL with TIR.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Controlled experimental framework implementing alternative trajectory filtering strategies for comparison: (1) high importance ratio filtering (masking trajectories exceeding ratio thresholds), (2) low token probability filtering (masking trajectories with minimum probabilities below thresholds), (3) stop-generation-on-void-without-filtering (terminating generation at void turns but including partial trajectories in loss), tracking gradient norms, training scores, and void turn ratios across conditions.

modules.name: Reasoning Pattern Analyzer
modules.description: Automated analysis of emergent multi-turn reasoning behaviors using a secondary LLM (e.g., Claude) to classify trajectories into patterns: cross-validation (multiple code blocks solving different aspects with verified results), progressive reasoning (sequential step-by-step code blocks building toward solution), and error correction (code blocks that retry after execution errors), computing frequency statistics for pattern comparison across methods.

modules.name: Experiment Infrastructure and Configuration
modules.description: Configuration management system with YAML-based hyperparameter specification (learning rate, clip ratios, batch sizes, GAE parameters, discount factors), experiment tracking with TensorBoard/Wandb integration for logging training dynamics (accuracy curves, gradient norms, response lengths, code use frequency, void turn ratios), model checkpoint saving/loading, and automated generation of comparison tables and training curve visualizations.
